sentences.text: Dated : 21-07-2023 Shri Upendra Yadav,
learned counsel for petitioner.
Shri V.P.S. Tomar, learned Panel Lawyer for State.

Heard on IA.No.90/2023, 1st application u/Sec.
389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant- Aman Kushwah.
Vide judgment dated 17.11.2022 passed in S.T. No.194/2019 by learned Special Judge (POCSO Act)
and 13th Additional Sessions Judge District Gwalior appellant has been convicted under Section 376(1) of IPC and sentenced to undergo 10 years RI with fine of Rs.5,000/- with default stipulation.
In brief facts of the case are that prosecutrix aged about 17 years lodged a handwritten complaint against the appellant alleging that she knows present appellant since last five months.
He used to work alongwith her maternal uncle Santosh.
They developed friendship because he used to come at the house of her maternal uncle.
They used to talk each other on mobile.
On 17.12.2018 present appellant came at the house of her maternal uncle.
She is residing at the house of her maternal uncle since last two years.
On 17.12.2018 present appellant after taking permission of her maternal grandmother, took her to Achleshwar Temple.
After darshan, he took her to Krishna Lodge Hotel situated at Nai Sadak where he forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her.
She did not disclose the incident to her family members.

After 5-6 days, present appellant told her that he took her obscene photographs and threatened her that if she would not make physical relations with her again, he would viral her photographs and thereafter viraled her photographs.
Thereafter prosecutrix disclosed the incident to her Naani.
On her complaint, after one and a half months the offence was registered.
After, investigation, charge-sheet in the matter has been filed.
After conclusion of trial, learned Trial Court convicted the appellant for the aforesaid offences.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the prosecutrix was the consenting party.
During trial, appellant has suffered incarceration of about more than 14 months.
Final hearing of the appeal will take time and they have a good case on merits.
the appellant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by the Court.
Therefore, prayer for suspension of sentence has been made.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
